gaps.sentence: The newspapers ___ the story about the minister's resignation.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'a story' meaning revealed it first
gaps.explanation: break a story is the journalism collocation meaning to be the first to report news.

gaps.sentence: There was ___ fog at the airport all morning.
gaps.explanation: thick fog (or dense fog) is the standard collocation; 'strong fog' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: Her talk really ___ home the urgency of the situation.
gaps.explanation: 'Drive something home' = make it fully understood.

gaps.sentence: Most children learn to ___ the time before they start school.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ the time (read a clock)
gaps.explanation: tell the time means to be able to read a clock; it is a fixed expression.

gaps.sentence: The crash left several passengers seriously ___.
gaps.explanation: seriously injured is the standard collocation describing bad injuries in accidents.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ losses of two million last year.
The ___ traffic added an hour to our journey.
gaps.explanation: heavy traffic means a lot of vehicles on the road; 'thick traffic' is not standard.

gaps.sentence: He was sent to prison for ___ the law.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'the law' (opposite of obeying it)
gaps.explanation: break the law means to commit a crime; after the preposition 'for' the -ing form is needed.
